verdict.rationale: Ente Auth has no explicit AI-training policy or opt-out. However, its documented end-to-end encrypted sync and backups (encrypted with a key derived from the user's password) and its offline 'Use without backups' mode mean the vendor structurally cannot read user codes, so it could not train on them. That protection is implied by the architecture rather than promised. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement or policy that user data is never used for AI/model training, a user-facing control or opt-out, and independent verification of the encryption claims.
